title: Move prepare out of the loop
summary: Reuse one statement with sqlite3_reset and sqlite3_clear_bindings instead of rebuilding it for every row.

turns.user: add_tags is slow. profiler says prepare_v2 is like half the time. posts can have hundreds of tags

assistant.body: Got it. Calling prepare_v2 on every pass parses the same SQL and compiles it to bytecode again each time. Build the statement once outside the loop, and use sqlite3_reset to put it back in its ready state before the next row. Note: reset does not forget bound values. A row with a NULL note never binds parameter 3, so it would silently get the previous row's note. sqlite3_clear_bindings sets every parameter back to NULL. That also clears post_id, so it is bound again inside the loop.

turns.user: you're ignoring what reset returns, is that fine?

assistant.body: Great question! sqlite3_reset returns the error of the previous sqlite3_step if that step failed. This loop checks the step first and breaks on anything but SQLITE_DONE, so by the time reset runs, the step before it has succeeded. In other words, reset always returns SQLITE_OK here. sqlite3_clear_bindings only ever returns SQLITE_OK too, so dropping both is safe.
